scope: Tests the distance function on hand-written pairs. Does NOT test the execution protocol's choice of entry point, which is where the output-free constraint is violated: see artifacts/final/OUTPUT_ORACLE_LEAK_AUDIT.json, 47 of 64 programs trace a self-test driver whose assert statements land in the exception features. A pass here is necessary, not sufficient.

tests.description: sum list: x*2 vs x*3 (same loop, different return value)
classify(x): returns string vs int (same branches taken)
fibonacci: fib(n) vs 2*fib(n) (same recursion depth, different values)
linear search: returns None vs -1 when not found (same path)
generator: yields x^2 vs x^3 (same iteration count, different values)
QuixBugs-style gcd: correct vs return a*2 (same control flow)
mergesort: identical algorithm, all variables renamed
binary search factory: two instances of same function (d=0.0 expected)
tests.note: Functions from the same factory share co_name='_bsearch', so anonymization assigns them the same index. Different co_name functions with same code would have different indices only if the indexing is not purely positional — this is documented as a known behavior: rename-invariance applies to variable renames, not function-name renames.

tests.description: double list: explicit loop vs list comprehension (style equivalence, d < 0.30 allowed)
tests.note: List comprehension creates a <listcomp> frame; some trace divergence is expected and acceptable
